title: Fancy_Bear_Incident_Response_fce
description: A sophisticated cyber espionage group known as Fancy Bear has been detected in your network. Your task is to investigate, analyze, and respond to this incident following the Incident Response profile.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Fancy Bear group is known for its sophisticated cyber espionage activities. They use backdoors for persistent access to compromised systems. The group is capable of lateral movement, exfiltration, and maintaining persistence. The malware family targets Windows, Linux, and macOS platforms.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: To access the sandbox in the cloud, use the following credentials: username: trainee, password: training123. Enter 'start' to begin.
levels.local_content: For local sandbox usage, use the following credentials: username: trainee, password: training123. Enter 'start' to begin.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring your network, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the target host. Investigate the host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running.
levels.solution: Check running services and their associated processes. The suspicious service running on port 4444 is bkd.service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and their associated processes.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Now that you've identified the suspicious service, determine how it is automatically started after reboot. This will help you understand the attacker's persistence mechanism.
levels.solution: Investigate systemd services and timers. The systemd timer responsible for starting the suspicious service is lab-checkin.timer.

levels.title: Lateral Movement Investigation
levels.content: Investigate if the attacker has moved laterally from the target host to other hosts in the network. Look for evidence of file transfers or remote execution.
levels.solution: Check for any services or processes responsible for transferring data between hosts. The service responsible for transferring data from target to next-target is payload-transfer.service.

hints.content: Check for any services or processes responsible for transferring data between hosts.
